verdict: No blocking correctness, compatibility, or complexity findings in the SDK optimization.
scope: Read-only source review, existing evidence inspection, benchmark consistency checks, and 7 independently rerun focused tests. No compiler rebuild or tracked source edits by reviewer; canonical compiler untouched.
metadata_proof: mo_frontend/typing.ml:3591-3642: intrinsic identity is recognized through promoted types; final inference calls specialize (pre-inference alone skips it), validates argument schema and concrete/opaque requirements, and records explicit type arguments. Source interpreter uses the same checked callee, instantiation, argument and result annotations (mo_interpreter/interpret.ml:636-656).

lowering/desugar.ml:173-194 copies specialization annotations with sequence/parenthesized argument semantics intact. ir/ir.ml:310 maps all three type-bearing fields using map_specialization; erase_typ_field.ml:84 and async.ml:237 use that mapping.

ir_def/check_ir.ml:757-774 checks argument/result subtyping, every metadata type, fresh specialization success and exact result type equality. pipeline.ml:766,776 checks desugaring and each transformation by default (flags.ml:33); explicit -no-check-ir intentionally opts out of compiler sanity checking.

compute_plugin.ml retains supplied value arity and matching Local/Returns callback argument/result calling conventions. These are value-dependent checks. Removed result recomputation depends only on already checked static metadata.
cursor_proof: compile.ml:9717-9739 evaluates length once, allocates with existing size overflow guard, resolves initial array forwarding, initializes all slots before any callback, applies allocation barrier, then writes exactly indices [0,length) with write_with_barrier. Cursor advances one 8-byte element per completed iteration.

Each invocation uses fresh Wasm locals; nested and recursive callbacks cannot overwrite its cursor. Zero length still initializes a valid empty array; early decoder return leaves every slot valid for later GC.

Local synchronous callbacks cannot suspend the surrounding frame. Actual GC sites are outer message/export cleanup; allocation may grow Wasm memory without changing linear-memory offsets. ICPerformGC is an internal IR constructor without a source producer. RTS write/allocation barriers mark or forward references and do not move the containing array.

No bounds, decoding, overflow, or value-dependent checks were removed. Arr.get retains idx bounds checking; Tuple.load_n already uses constant offsets; Object.load_idx_raw retains hash lookup required by record width subtyping.
callback_tuple_loader_proof: Backend.Call.local checks fully instantiated synchronous local function metadata, evaluates closure then arguments exactly once, dispatches with input/output sequence arities, and boxes multiresults only when providing the managed callback result.

ComputePlugins.compile validates Tuple n only against normalized known tuple result shape (n=0 or n>=2), preserving opaque values and ordinary stack representation adaptation. Existing tests assert no allocation for direct pair/triple/unit results and managed retention for stored tuples.

Plugin declarations/API/ABI remain unchanged (ABI 1). Native Dynlink checks compiler interface compatibility; registration validates ABI/names/duplicates; runtime linker validates imports and signatures, shared Wasm64 memory/table, forbidden globals/start functions, and unresolved imports. Packaging tests cover these boundaries.
